rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ancient accounts of Cyrus marching north to suppress unrest support identifying his iron-and-stone barrier with the Qur’anic dam at Darial between two mountains.
rows.anchor: وقد ذكر المؤرخون من القدماء كهرودوت اليوناني سير كورش إلى شمال إيران لإخماد نوائر فتن اشتعلت هناك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nearby rivers bearing Cyrus’s western name and the name Kur near Tbilisi further support the identification.
rows.anchor: وجود نهر بالقرب منه يسمى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Josephus mentions the northern Caucasus barrier; it is not the Derbent wall, built later by Khosrow Anushirwan, which used no iron.
rows.anchor: اليهودي المؤرخ عند ذكر رحلته إلى شمال قفقاز وليس هو الحائط الموجود في باب الأبواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yajuj and Majuj are the Mongols: their names appear to derive through Hebrew from Chinese Mengkuk, alongside related forms Mongol and Mughal.
rows.anchor: فإن الكلمة بالتكلم الصيني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Mongols were a large northern and eastern Asian people who raided China, the Caucasus, Iran, Europe, and Rome; biblical material also places the corrupt nation in the far north.
rows.anchor: وقد تقدم أيضا أن المستفاد من كتب العهد العتيق أن هذه الأمة المفسدة من سكنة أقاصي الشمال

rows.speaker: بعض مشايخي
rows.claim: Some of the author’s teachers place Dhul-Qarnayn in a human cycle before the present one to accommodate reports of repeated deaths and resurrections, ascension, and command over clouds and natural forces.
rows.anchor: سمعته عن بعض مشايخي أنه من أهل بعض الأدوار السابقة على هذه الدورة الإنسانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Despite objections to details, the Cyrus-and-Mongol account fits the verses more clearly and is more acceptable than competing identifications; the teacher’s account overtrusts extraordinary reports.
rows.anchor: لكنه أوضح انطباقا على الآيات وأقرب إلى القبول من غيره

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير والمؤرخون
rows.claim: Most exegetes and historians identify Yajuj and Majuj as a large northern Asian nation, and some apply their end-time devastation to the Mongol invasions of the seventh Islamic century.
rows.anchor: وأكثرهم على أن يأجوج ومأجوج أمة كبيرة في شمال آسيا، وقد طبق جمع منهم ما أخبر به القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This identification leaves the barrier unexplained: the Mongols crossed broad regions, so no Qur’anic wall can be located as the barrier they broke through to reach those lands.
rows.anchor: لكنهم أهملوا البحث عن أمر السد من جهة خروجهم منه وحل مشكلته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If another historical people is intended, no iron barrier has been found that confined a large nation for millennia, especially when modern land, sea, and air routes connect the world.
rows.anchor: فأين هذا السد المشيد بالحديد ومن صفته أنه يحبس أمة كبيرة منذ ألوف من السنين

rows.speaker: لسان العرب
rows.claim: One lexical sense of dakka is humbled or brought low, as in the expression for a humbled mountain.
rows.anchor: قال في لسان العرب وجبل دك ذليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dakka means the wall is rendered ineffective and disregarded as expanding transport and communication let people cross the earth and attack any community.
rows.anchor: والمراد بجعل السد دكاء جعله ذليلا لا يعبأ بأمره ولا ينتفع به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promised event is human civilization’s rise and worldwide connectivity, which makes barriers unable to confine peoples; the parallel passage speaks of Yajuj and Majuj being opened without mentioning a wall.
rows.anchor: فحقيقة هذا الوعد هو الوعد برقي المجتمع البشري في مدنيته

rows.speaker: الصحاح
rows.claim: Other lexical senses of dakka are burying a well with soil or reducing mountains to clay mounds.
rows.anchor: ففي الصحاح دككت الركي - وهو البئر - دفنته بالتراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wall may have been buried by storms or submerged through geological changes in sea levels, but the author prefers the explanation based on modern mobility.
rows.anchor: فمن الممكن أن يحتمل أن السد من جملة أبنية العهود القديمة التي ذهبت مدفونة تحت التراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bighya means seeking and hawl means changing or turning away; the remainder of the verse is straightforward.
rows.anchor: البغي الطلب، والحول التحول، والباقي ظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promised paradise is also described as containing what its people desire and further gifts, with hidden joys and unexpected divine recompense in other verses.
rows.anchor: لهم ما يشاؤن فيها ولدينا مزيد

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: In response to Ibn al-Kawwa’s question about the greatest losers, Ali identifies them as the sinful people of Quraysh.
rows.anchor: عن أبي الطفيل قال سمعت علي بن أبي طالب وسأله ابن الكوا فقال

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: A report through al-Ayyashi says the losers are People of the Book who disbelieved and innovated; it adds that the people of the River are not far from them.
rows.anchor: قام ابن الكوا إلى أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام فقال أخبرني عن قول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author notes another report identifying the losers as Christians.
rows.anchor: أقول وروي أنهم النصاري، القمي عن أبي جعفر

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: Al-Qummi and al-Tabarsi transmit that the losers are People of the Book.
rows.anchor: القمي عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام والطبرسي في الاحتجاج عن علي عليه السلام أنهم أهل الكتاب

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: A report transmitted by Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim identifies them as monks who secluded themselves in pillars.
rows.anchor: عن أبي خميصة عبد الله بن قيس عن علي عليه السلام أنهم الرهبان الذين حبسوا أنفسهم في السواري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These reports are applications rather than the verse’s original referent: the surrounding passage addresses idolaters, and its description in 18:106 fits them better than other groups; al-Qummi’s Jewish-to-Kharijite account is unsound.
rows.anchor: والروايات جميعا من قبيل الجري، والآيتان واقعتان في سياق متصل وجه الكلام فيه مع المشركين

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: A report from Ali calls Firdaws the summit of everything and the highest part of Paradise, reserved for Muhammad and his family.
rows.anchor: عن الحارث عن علي عليه السلام قال لكل شيء ذروة وذروة الجنة الفردوس

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: The Prophet instructs believers to ask for Firdaws, the middle and highest part of Paradise, above which is the Throne and from which its rivers spring.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse independently declares that God’s words cannot be exhausted; it may have been revealed alone, though it also coheres with the whole surah.
rows.anchor: بيان الآية بيان مستقل لسعة كلمات الله تعالى وعدم قبولها النفاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah’s stories reveal hidden divine realities: the sleepers awaken, Khidr explains the meanings behind actions that perplexed Moses, and Dhul-Qarnayn’s wall restrains corruption; God’s words disclose such aims without end.
rows.anchor: أمور تحتها حقائق واسرار وبالحقيقة كلمات تكشف عن مقاصد إلهية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its placement after the surah’s completed discussion resembles someone ending a long account by saying it has no end and stopping with what has been presented.
rows.anchor: والآية في وقوعها بعد استيفاء السورة ما استوفتها من البيان بوجه مثل قول القائل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’anic word can mean either a sentence or a single term; its use for God’s utterance and decrees is illustrated by several verses.
rows.anchor: الكلمة تطلق على الجملة كما تطلق على المفرد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A word is called a word because it signifies God; Christ is called God’s word for this reason.
rows.anchor: وإنما تسمى كلمة لكونها آية دالة عليه تعالى ومن هنا سمى المسيح كلمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every existent thing and event is a divine word as a sign, though Qur’anic usage especially marks clear, immutable signs and decrees, such as Jesus and irrevocable judgments.
rows.anchor: ما من عين يوجد أو واقعة تقع إلا وهي من حيث كونها آية دالة عليه كلمة منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Interpreting God’s words here as His knowledge, capabilities, promises, or similar enumerated meanings is unsound.
rows.anchor: أن حمل الكلمات في الآية على معلوماته أو مقدوراته تعالى أو مواعده لأهل الثواب والعقاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the sea’s water were ink to record the divine signs it would run out before they did; adding another sea would also run out first.
rows.anchor: أي فرقمت الكلمات وأثبتت من حيث دلالتها بذاك البحر المأخوذ مدادا لنفد البحر

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some interpreters take another sea like it to mean an unlimited class of seas, since adding any finite number cannot encompass the infinite knowledge they posit.
rows.anchor: وذكر بعضهم أن المراد بمثله جنس المثل لا مثل واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That explanation is right in conclusion but not because finite quantities cannot measure an infinity: the issue is that realities exceed measures, and no sea particle can fully record its own signification.
rows.anchor: وما ذكره حق لكن لا لحديث التناهي واللاتناهي وإن كانت الكلمات غير متناهية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating sea and using the explicit my Lord instead of a pronoun reinforces the statement; specifying Lord and attaching it to the speaker also honors him.
rows.anchor: وضع الظاهر موضع المضمر والنكتة فيه التثبيت والتأكيد

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: A report from Abu Basir says God’s speech has no end or limit and never ceases.
rows.anchor: عن أبي بصير عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام في الآية قال أخبرك أن كلام الله ليس له آخر ولا غاية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah’s closing verse gathers the three foundations of religion: divine oneness, prophethood, and resurrection.
rows.anchor: وقد جمعت أصول الدين الثلاثة وهي التوحيد والنبوة والمعاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet’s first qualification confines him to ordinary human nature, rejecting claims to divinity or hidden power that motivated demands for miracles; revelation is the exception.
rows.anchor: القصر الأول قصره صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم في البشرية المماثلة لبشرية الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second qualification confines divinity to one God, and the command to do good deeds is a concise call to religion and worshipping God alone.
rows.anchor: والقصر الثاني قصر الإله الذي هو إلههم في إله واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Righteous action follows hope of returning to God, because without judgment and recompense there would be no motive for religious belief or practice.
rows.anchor: إذ لولا الحساب والجزاء لم يكن للأخذ بالدين والتلبس بالاعتقاد والعمل موجب يدعو إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Belief in one God rules out associating partners in worship, since oneness in all divine attributes includes exclusive worthiness of worship.
rows.anchor: لأن الاعتقاد بالوحدانية مع الاشتراك في العمل متناقضان لا يجتمعان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse bases action on hope rather than certainty of the meeting because even its possibility requires caution to avert possible harm.
rows.anchor: لأن احتماله كاف في وجوب التحذر منه لوجوب دفع الضرر المحتمل

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes meeting the Lord as a hoped-for meeting of honor rather than a certain encounter.
rows.anchor: وربما قيل إن المراد باللقاء لقاء الكرامة وهو مرجو لا مقطوع به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hope of meeting God follows from His being the sole God: divine perfection, truth, and justice entail the return and judgment of His servants.
rows.anchor: لأن رجوع العباد إلى الله سبحانه من تمام معنى الألوهية

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report says Jundub ibn Zuhayr enjoyed praise for worship and increased his prayer, fasting, and charity to gain people’s approval, whereupon the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال كان جندب بن زهير إذا صلى أو صام أو تصدق فذكر بخير ارتاح له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Parallel reports omit Jundub’s name and should be read as applying the verse to the case; it is unlikely that a whole surah’s conclusion was revealed for one specific incident.
rows.anchor: وينبغي أن يحمل على انطباق الآية على المورد فمن المستبعد أن ينزل خاتمة سورة من السور لسبب خاص بنفسها

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet quotes God as saying He accepts only work done sincerely for Him and leaves work shared with another creature to that creature.
rows.anchor: عن أبي حاتم عن سعيد بن جبير في الآية قال النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم إن ربكم يقول أنا خير شريك

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: A report from Abu Abd Allah says God, the best partner, accepts only work made sincere for Him.
rows.anchor: عن علي بن سالم عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال قال الله تبارك وتعالى أنا خير شريك

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Another report says a deed done for God and someone else belongs to the one for whom it was done, not to God.
rows.anchor: وفي رواية أخرى عنه عليه السلام قال إن الله يقول أنا خير شريك

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet calls prayer, fasting, or charity done for show forms of association, then recites this verse.
rows.anchor: عن شداد بن أوس قال سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

rows.speaker: زرارة وحمران
rows.claim: Abu Ja‘far and Abu Abd Allah say that including anyone’s approval in an act done for God’s mercy and the afterlife makes the act associational.
rows.anchor: عن زرارة وحمران عن أبي جعفر وأبي عبد الله عليهما السلام قالا لو أن عبدا عمل عملا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The many Sunni and Shi‘i reports use shirk for hidden association, which does not negate basic faith but diminishes its perfection.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالشرك فيها الشرك الخفي غير المنافي لأصل الإيمان بل لكماله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reports’ hidden association is covered by the inner meaning of the verse about most people believing in God while associating others with Him, not by its original revelation.
rows.anchor: فالآية تشمله بباطنها لا بتنزيلها

rows.speaker: أبو حكيم
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet declared that the ending of Surat al-Kahf alone would suffice for his community; the author says its explanation was already given.
rows.anchor: عن أبي حكيم قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah’s purpose is warning and glad tidings, illustrated through the stories of prophets granted divine friendship, prophethood, truthfulness, and sincerity.
rows.anchor: هو التبشير والإنذار غير أنه ساق الكلام في ذلك سوقا بديعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah contrasts humble, grateful predecessors with descendants who abandon devotion for desire and error, while allowing repentant believers to return to the blessed path.
rows.anchor: لكن أخلافهم أعرضوا عن ذلك وأهملوا أمر التوجه إلى ربهم واتبعوا الشهوات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Stories serve as examples for a general division into the blessed, the erring, and repentant believers, followed by their respective reward and punishment; the surah rebuts denials of resurrection, divine offspring, and worship of idols.
rows.anchor: فالسورة تقسم الناس إلى ثلاث طوائف الذين أنعم الله عليهم من النبيين وأهل الإجتباء والهدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah is Meccan, as its themes show and commentators unanimously report.
rows.anchor: والسورة مكية بلا ريب تدل على ذلك مضامين آياتها وقد نقل على ذلك اتفاق المفسرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disjointed-letter openings relate their shared letters to shared surah themes; Maryam parallels Sad in prophetic stories and shares Ya with Yasin and Ayn with al-Shura.
rows.anchor: السور القرآنية المصدرة بالحروف المقطعة لا تخلو من ارتباط بين مضامينها وبين تلك الحروف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the opening phrase, dhikr is the predicate of an omitted subject and the verbal noun means its object; the mercy is God’s response to Zechariah’s prayer, explained by the next clause.
rows.anchor: ظاهر السياق أن الذكر خبر لمبتدأ محذوف والمصدر بمعنى المفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The time clause attaches to God’s mercy; nida ordinarily means calling aloud, unlike private supplication, but can be hidden when spoken where people cannot hear.
rows.anchor: والنداء والمناداة الجهر بالدعوة خلاف المناجاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description of the call as hidden is compatible with speaking aloud in private, as Zechariah later leaves the prayer niche to address his people.
rows.anchor: لإمكان الجهر بالدعوة في خلاء من الناس لا يسمعون معه الدعوة

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say Zechariah used the word calling because his sins and poor condition made him feel distant from God, like someone fearing punishment.
rows.anchor: وقيل إن العناية في التعبير بالنداء أنه تصور نفسه بعيدا منه تعالى بذنوبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zechariah’s description of weakness prepares his request for an heir; beginning with Lord is an entreaty, while inna stresses the certainty of his need.
rows.anchor: تمهيد لما سيسأله وهو قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wahn means weakness and loss of strength; he attributes it to the bones as the body’s support, using a singular generic noun before detailing the condition.
rows.anchor: والوهن هو الضعف ونقصان القوة وقد نسبه إلى العظم لأنه الدعامة

rows.speaker: المجمع
rows.claim: The metaphor of gray hair spreading across the head like the rays or flames of fire is among the Qur’an’s finest images.
rows.anchor: قال في المجمع وقوله { واشتعل الرأس شيبا } من أحسن الاستعارات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shiqā means deprivation of good or possibly deprivation itself; Zechariah says his past prayers were answered rather than leaving him deprived or disappointed.
rows.anchor: وكنت سعيدا بسبب دعائي إياك كلما دعوتك استجبت لي من غير أن تشقيني

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: An alternative construes the prayer as God’s call to worship: Zechariah had not been wretched by resisting, but remained obedient and sincere; the author prefers the prayer-as-request reading.
rows.anchor: مصدر مضاف إلى الفاعل، والمعنى لم أكن بدعوتك إياي إلى العبودية والطاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating Lord inside the clause between subject and predicate is exceptionally eloquent, as in his later request to make the child pleasing.
rows.anchor: من البلاغة ما لا يقدر بقدر، ونظيره قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-mawali may mean paternal uncles and cousins, agnates, clan, or heirs; in any case it means kin other than direct offspring, and fearing their actions after his death euphemistically expresses fear of dying childless.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالموالي العمومة وبنو العم، وقيل الكلالة وقيل العصبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A barren woman cannot bear children, and describing his wife as barren in the past tense suggests she was already beyond childbearing age.
rows.anchor: العاقر المرأة التي لا تلد يقال امرأة عاقر لا تلد ورجل عاقر لا يولد له ولد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Describing his wife as barren in the past tense indicates that she had already passed childbearing age; the clause is circumstantial and explains his fear of successors inheriting after his death.
rows.anchor: وفي التعبير بقوله { وكانت امرأتي } دلالة على أن امرأته على كونها عاقرا جازت حين الدعاء سن الولادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording can be analyzed as two or three units: God had answered Zechariah throughout life, and his wife’s barrenness left him fearing successors after his death.
rows.anchor: فمجموع ما مهدة للدعاء يؤل إلى فصلين أحدهما أن الله سبحانه عوده الاستجابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary’s devotion and extraordinary favor prompted Zechariah’s prayer: he hoped for a successor with similar nearness to God.
rows.anchor: ولا يرتاب المتدبر في الآيتين أن الذي دعا زكريا ودفعه إلى دعائه بما دعا هو ما شاهده من حال مريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The request for good progeny in Al Imran corresponds to the request for an heir in Maryam.
rows.anchor: فقوله في سورة آل عمران { رب هب لي من لدنك ذرية طيبة } بحذاء قوله في سورة مريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description of the progeny as good corresponds to asking that the child be pleasing, expressing the devotion and favor seen in Mary.
rows.anchor: وقوله هناك { طيبة } بحذاء قوله هنا { واجعله رب رضيا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parallel wording confirms the requested heir is a son of Zechariah’s own loins; asking God to grant an outsider would not fit language implying possession.
rows.anchor: على أن التعبير بمثل { هب لي } المشعر بنوع من الملك لا يستقيم في سائر الناس من الأجانب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zechariah also recalled his old age, his wife’s age and barrenness, disfavored relatives, and God’s past response to his prayers before asking for good progeny.
rows.anchor: ثم ذكر ما هو عليه من الشيب ونفاد القوة وما عليه امرأته من كبر السن والعقر وله موال لا يرتضيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wali denotes the child as heir; inheritance ordinarily means inheriting the deceased’s property, and the term’s broad sense is narrowed by its pairing with wali and the preceding fear of successors.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالوراثة وراثة ما تركه الميت من الأموال وأمتعة الحياة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inheritance of prophethood is untenable: lineage does not transmit prophethood, Mary’s devotion gives no reason to request it, and making a prophet pleasing would be redundant or lesser.
rows.anchor: وأما قول من قال إن المراد به وراثة النبوة وإنه طلب من ربه أن يهب له ولدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taking pleasing to mean approved by people conflicts with its unrestricted wording and does not fit what prompted the prayer.
rows.anchor: وكذا احتمال أن يكون المراد بالرضي المرضي عند الناس لمنافاته إطلاق المرضي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inheritance of knowledge also fails: Mary’s devotion does not motivate asking for an heir to knowledge, while make him pleasing already covers beneficial knowledge and good action.
rows.anchor: والقول بأن المراد بالوراثة وراثة العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inheritance of piety, closeness, or divine favor is ill-suited: he would ask for a child like Mary, not one inheriting his own station, and it makes no sense to fear cousins acquiring piety or nearness to God.
rows.anchor: على أنه لا يلائمه قوله { وإني خفت الموالي من ورائي } إذ ظاهر السياق أنه يطلب ولدا يرثه

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say Zechariah feared his relatives would succeed him among the Israelites and fail to guide them well.
rows.anchor: وقول بعضهم إن مواليه عليه السلام كانوا شرار بني إسرائيل فخاف أن لا يحسنوا خلافته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If succession means divine inward authority, it is not inherited and only goes to fit recipients; if it means worldly rule, it is property-like, not a distinct spiritual inheritance.
rows.anchor: فهي مما لا يورث بالنسب قطعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yahya held no kingship or worldly rule to inherit, and Israel had no king in their time because Rome ruled them.
rows.anchor: ولم يكن لبني إسرائيل ملك في زمن زكريا ويحيى بل كانت الروم مستولية عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An objection says detached, holy souls such as Zechariah could not care about wealth enough to fear its inheritance or ask for an heir to preserve it.
rows.anchor: فإن قلت يؤيد حمل الوراثة في الآية على وراثة العلم ونحوه دون المال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The objection mistakes the request’s primary aim: he asks for a child, as Al Imran and the prayer not to be left alone show; inheritance merely identifies the general wali as a child.
rows.anchor: فليس المقصود من قوله { وليا يرثني } بالقصد الأول إلا طلب الولد

rows.speaker: المعترض
rows.claim: The objection maintains that Zechariah’s purpose was to uphold divine law and preserve prophethood among his descendants.
rows.anchor: فليس قصده عليه السلام من مسألة الولد سوى إجراء أحكام الله تعالى وترويج الشريعة وبقاء النبوة في أولاده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is unnecessary to suppose Zechariah feared relatives would misuse an inheritance: the deceased bears no blame for the heir’s lawful disposal, and he could have given away his property beforehand.
rows.anchor: إذا مات الرجل وانتقل ماله بالوراثة إلى آخر صار المال مال الوارث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without inheritance of property as the clarifying clue, the text would not identify the requested wali as a child; inheritance of knowledge, prophethood, worship, or grace does not itself imply a son.
rows.anchor: ولولا أن المراد به الوراثة المالية وأنها قرينة معينة لم يبق في الكلام ما يدل على طلب الولد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Financial inheritance is not the primary purpose of the prayer, but it confirms the child sought; neither inheritance nor fear of successors proves attachment to worldly luxury.
rows.anchor: فليست مقصودة بالقصد الأول وإنما هي قرينة معينة لكون المراد بالولي هو الولد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wanting a child is a natural human disposition that divine law neither abolishes nor condemns, and Qur’anic prayers praise the desire for righteous offspring.
rows.anchor: والشرائع الإلهية لم تبطل هذا الحكم الفطري ولا ذمت هذه الداعية الغريزية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative report says Zechariah saw Mary receive winter fruit in summer and summer fruit in winter, prompting him to hope God could grant him a child despite old age and barrenness.
rows.anchor: فقد ورد في بعض الآثار أن زكريا كان يجد عند مريم فواكه في غير موسمها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The context does not establish that Mary’s provision was out-of-season fruit or that it prompted the request; it emphasizes her special divine favor beyond ordinary causes.
rows.anchor: لا دليل من جهة السياق اللفظي على كون المراد بالرزق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if the report is accepted, it explains hope for a child, followed by the request that the child be righteous and pleasing; inheritance marks the child and cannot mean nonhereditary spiritual stations without an unstated clue.
rows.anchor: ولو سلم ذلك كان مقتضاه أن ينبعث زكريا بالقصد الأول إلى طلب الذرية والولد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The announcement omits an abbreviated response, understood as We answered him and called: the parallel account says God granted Yahya.
rows.anchor: فاستجبنا له ووهبنا له يحيى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al Imran says angels announced Yahya while Zechariah prayed, showing that the announcement was mediated by angels; the later wording your Lord said confirms this.
rows.anchor: وتشهد آية آل عمران على أن قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God named him Yahya, and no one before bore that same name; alternatively, samiyyan means an equal or counterpart, as in the later question whether anyone is God’s namesake.
rows.anchor: وأنه لم يسم بهذا الأسم قبله أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yahya receives unique descriptions: wisdom as a child, leadership and chastity, and peace at birth, death, and resurrection; Jesus shared them but was born later, though they were cousins.
rows.anchor: نعته في كلامه بنعوت لم ينعت به أحدا من أنبيائه وأوليائه قبله

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Ghulam denotes a young male at the stage when a moustache appears, and can also describe reaching sexual maturity.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب الغلام الطار الشارب يقال غلام بين الغلومة والغلومية

rows.speaker: المجمع
rows.claim: Atiyy and asiyy describe a person dried and hardened by time; reaching this state indicates that Zechariah’s sexual capacity and prospect of fathering a child had ended.
rows.anchor: وقال في المجمع العتي والعسي بمعنى يقال عتا يعتو عتوا وعتيا وعسا يعسو عسوا وعسيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zechariah’s question about having a son expresses amazement and asks for details to settle his mind, not disbelief or denial of the announcement.
rows.anchor: مبني على استعجاب البشرى واستفسار خصوصياتها دون الإستبعاد والإنكار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person surprised by unexpected news may ask for details to calm initial agitation while remaining certain of its truth.
rows.anchor: فإن الخطورات النفسانية ربما لا تنقطع مع وجود العلم والإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zechariah’s question, while believing the promise, parallels Abraham’s request to see how God revives the dead: both seek reassurance amid wonder.
rows.anchor: وإذ قال إبراهيم رب أرني كيف تحيي الموتى قال أو لم تؤمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kadhālika is reported speech meaning the matter is indeed as promised; God’s statement that it is easy explains that His will cannot be thwarted, even in creating a child for the elderly couple.
rows.anchor: مقول القول وهو خبر مبتدأ محذوف والتقدير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reminder that God created Zechariah when he was nothing gives a prior example of creation that removes the apparent difficulty.
rows.anchor: بيان لبعض مصاديق الخلق الذي يرفع به الاستعجاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternative parses attach thus to a later clause or address the Prophet rather than Zechariah; the context does not support them.
rows.anchor: وتلك وجوه لا يساعد عليها السياق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zechariah asks for a sign to distinguish true angelic revelation from a satanic suggestion; prophets are divinely protected from Satan.
rows.anchor: وهو عليه السلام إنما سأل الآية ليتميز به الحق من الباطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sign is inability to speak to people for three days while remaining healthy and able to remember God; the inability is expressed by naming its consequence, and the nights include their days.
rows.anchor: فالمراد بعدم تكليم الناس عدم القدرة على تكليمهم

rows.speaker: المجمع
rows.claim: Mihrab is so named because a worshipper faces it as a warrior defending prayer against Satan; it originally meant a protected chamber for notables.
rows.anchor: وسمي المحراب محرابا لأن المتوجه إليه في صلاته كالمحارب للشيطان

rows.speaker: المجمع
rows.claim: Wahy means conveying meaning secretly and swiftly, associated with the call hurry, hurry.
rows.anchor: وقال الإيحاء إلقاء المعنى إلى النفس في خفية بسرعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taking the book with strength means committing seriously to its teachings in both knowledge and practice; the omitted transition is that after Yahya was granted, God commanded him to take it firmly.
rows.anchor: أن المراد من أخذ الكتاب بقوة التحقق بما فيه من المعارف والعمل بما فيه من الأحكام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The book is likely the Torah, or it and earlier prophetic books, since the Torah contained the law in force at that time.
rows.anchor: فإن الكتاب الذي كان يشتمل على الشريعة يومئذ هو التوراة

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Interpreters gloss hukm as understanding, reason, wisdom, service etiquette, insight, or prophethood.
rows.anchor: فسر الحكم بالفهم وبالعقل وبالحكمة وبمعرفة آداب الخدمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hukm cannot mean prophethood because the Qur’an distinguishes judgment from prophethood, and the other proposed senses lack linguistic or contextual evidence.
rows.anchor: أن الحكم غير النبوة، فتفسير الحكم بالنبوة ليس على ما ينبغي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parallel pairing of scripture, wisdom, and purification suggests hukm is knowledge of true divine realities, including what lies beyond ordinary perception; Yahya received it as a child before puberty.
rows.anchor: أن المراد بالحكم العلم بالمعارف الحقة الإلهية وانكشاف ما هو تحت أستار الغيب

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Hanan means tenderness and compassion and is associated with mercy.
rows.anchor: ولكون الإشفاق لا ينفك من الرحمة عبر عن الرحمة بالحنان

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Hanan is interpreted as mercy, perhaps prophethood or divine friendship, or as love from people, compassion toward them, or God’s special tenderness toward Yahya.
rows.anchor: وفسر الحنان في الآية بالرحمة ولعل المراد بها النبوة أو الولاية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because hanan is from God and lies outside ordinary causes, the context favors a special divine attraction and bond between Yahya and his Lord, setting aside readings as popular affection or his own compassion for people.
rows.anchor: أن المراد به نوع عطف وانجذاب خاص إلهي بينه وبين ربه غير مألوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakat fundamentally means sound growth; it may describe God’s care nurturing Yahya or Yahya’s own love and attraction toward God, with growth of the spirit.
rows.anchor: والأصل في معناه النمو الصالح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakat is not best read as blessing, charity, or purity from sins; its basic sense of beneficial growth fits the surrounding description better.
rows.anchor: ومن هنا يظهر وهن ما قيل إن المراد بالزكاة البركة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taqi means guarding oneself from God’s prohibitions and their punishment; barr means kind treatment of parents, and jabbar is arrogant, refusing others’ rights while imposing one’s will.
rows.anchor: والبر بفتح الباء صفة مشبهة من البر بكسر الباء وهو الإحسان

rows.speaker: المجمع
rows.claim: Jabbar describes someone who recognizes no claim against himself; the word also applies to a palm tree beyond reach.
rows.anchor: قال في المجمع الذي لا يرى لأحد عليه حقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asi fundamentally means refusal or disobedience; the three clauses describe Yahya’s relations with God, his parents, and other people, respectively.
rows.anchor: مسوقة لبيان جوامع أحواله بالنسبة إلى الخالق والمخلوق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asi should not be restricted to disobedience toward God; in context Yahya was gentle, humble, helpful to the weak, and guiding toward repentance among people.
rows.anchor: أن تفسير بعضهم لقوله { عصيا } بقوله أي عاصيا لربه ليس على ما ينبغي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Salam means a state in which what one encounters is fitting and unfeared, unlike amn, which only means absence of feared harm; its indefinite form conveys grandeur.
rows.anchor: وتنكير السلام لإفادة التفخيم أي سلام فخيم عليه مما يكرهه في هذه الأيام الثلاثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The three days open distinct worlds: birth brings earthly safety, death brings bliss in the intermediate realm, and resurrection brings true life without fatigue.
rows.anchor: فسلام عليه يوم ولد فلا يمسه مكروه في الدنيا يزاحم سعادته

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say the added word alive signals that Yahya will be killed as a martyr.
rows.anchor: للدلالة على أنه سيقتل شهيدا
